options.d: Workers who sit all day also reported more eye strain than workers who use standing mats.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-023.explanation: If walking breaks, not the mat, explain the tightness gap, buying mats for all desks will not deliver the claimed relief.

distractorExplanations.a: Scuffing is a maintenance issue, not a challenge to the causal claim.
distractorExplanations.b: Prior ownership does not show that mats fail to reduce tightness.
distractorExplanations.d: Eye strain is a different symptom; it neither explains nor undercuts the back-tightness gap.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-024.prompt: After Oakridge banned feeding deer in yards, vehicle collisions with deer rose the next winter. Opponents say the ban failed. Which finding, if true, most helps the town show the ban was not the cause of the rise?

options.a: Some residents kept leaving birdseed in their yards that deer also ate after the ban.
options.b: Wildlife cameras still recorded deer on Oakridge lawns after dusk throughout that winter.
options.c: The fine for feeding deer was smaller than the fine for overnight street parking.
options.d: Neighboring towns without a feeding ban saw similar collision increases that winter.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-024.explanation: A parallel rise where feeding stayed legal points to a shared winter factor rather than Oakridge's ban as the cause of more collisions.

distractorExplanations.a: Continued feeding would, if anything, weaken the ban's implementation, not clear it of causing collisions.
distractorExplanations.b: Deer still on lawns speaks to compliance, not to whether the ban caused the crash spike.
distractorExplanations.c: Relative fine size does not identify the cause of the collision spike.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-025.prompt: Planners promoting walk-up apartments over shops argue that evening pedestrian counts rise where housing sits above cafes, cutting car errands. A comparison city that built housing without ground-floor retail saw evening walks rise only on streets that already had corner stores. Delivery vans then clustered on the storeless blocks. Which statement is best supported?

options.a: Density lifts walking mainly where daily goods are already within a short walk.
options.b: Delivery vans appear only in cities that prohibit ground-floor cafes under housing.
options.c: Evening pedestrian counts fall wherever apartments are built above cafes and shops.
options.d: Corner stores reduce walking because shoppers drive from one store to the next.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-025.explanation: The storeless housing blocks failed to raise evening walks and drew vans, while mixed streets gained pedestrians. That pattern ties walking gains to nearby daily goods, not to housing mass alone.

distractorExplanations.b: Vans clustered on storeless blocks; the text does not restrict vans to cafe-ban cities.
distractorExplanations.c: The argument's own examples include rising counts on mixed streets, not a universal fall.
distractorExplanations.d: Corner-store streets gained walkers; the text does not say stores induce driving between them.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-026.prompt: A clinic newsletter says a daily cup of kefir 'improves immunity' because regular drinkers reported fewer winter colds than non-drinkers. Which finding, if true, most weakens the causal claim?

options.a: Kefir brands vary noticeably in tartness and probiotic count from one batch to the next.
options.b: Kefir drinkers were also more likely to vaccinate and to stay home when symptomatic.
options.c: Most drinkers first learned about kefir from the clinic newsletter rather than from a doctor.
options.d: Some non-drinkers said they avoided kefir because dairy products upset their stomachs.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-026.explanation: Vaccination and staying home are independent cold-reducing behaviors that can create the reported gap without kefir causing immunity.

distractorExplanations.a: Tartness variation does not explain the cold-count difference.
distractorExplanations.c: Where drinkers heard about kefir does not create or explain a gap in reported colds.
distractorExplanations.d: Lactose as a reason for abstaining does not show that drinkers' fewer colds are non-causal.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-027.prompt: Advocates say raising the city living wage will cut poverty because every covered worker's hourly rate will rise. Which consideration most weakens that prediction?

options.a: The living-wage ordinance was drafted by a bipartisan task force of council members.
options.b: Some covered employers already pay their workers more than the proposed hourly floor.
options.c: Hours may be cut, and uncovered contractors may replace some covered jobs.
options.d: Poverty statistics for the city are published only once a year, after a long delay.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-027.explanation: If hours fall or work shifts to uncovered contractors, a higher hourly floor need not raise annual earnings enough to cut poverty.

distractorExplanations.a: The drafters' party mix does not address the earnings mechanism.
distractorExplanations.b: Employers already above the floor are unaffected; that does not show covered workers will lose hours.
distractorExplanations.d: Publication frequency is a measurement detail, not a weakening of the predicted poverty drop.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-028.prompt: Health officials want a per-ounce levy on bottled sweet tea to cut sugar intake. Which finding, if true, most strengthens the case that the levy will reduce consumption?

options.a: Many grocers find bottled sweet tea cheaper to stock and display than sparkling water.
options.b: Tourists passing through the airport buy a large share of the bottled sweet tea sold in the city.
options.c: The levy's revenue will be earmarked for children's dental clinics rather than for school lunch programs.
options.d: A similar city's equivalent levy shifted shoppers to unsweetened tea, with little cross-border buying.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-028.explanation: A peer city's substitution toward unsweetened tea, without leakage across the border, is direct evidence that a like levy can cut sweet-tea intake.

distractorExplanations.a: Relative stocking cost does not show that buyers will cut sugar ounces.
distractorExplanations.b: Airport tourist purchases could leak around a neighborhood levy, which would weaken, not strengthen.
distractorExplanations.c: Revenue earmarks affect clinics, not the price-consumption link.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-029.prompt: When a non-native vine covered a floodplain forest, native understory herbs vanished and songbird nests failed more often, apparently because cats hunted more easily in the simplified layer. After a five-year pull program, herbs returned in patches, but vine fragments resprouted from root crowns left in wet soil. Bird nesting success recovered only in patches where herbs exceeded a cover threshold. Which statement is best supported?

options.a: Pulling the vine restores nesting only where herb cover also rebounds past a threshold.
options.b: Cats permanently abandon a floodplain forest as soon as any vine stems are pulled from it.
options.c: Root-crown resprouts show that the vine cannot establish itself in wet floodplain soil.
options.d: Native herbs outcompete the vine on their own even where no pulling takes place.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-029.explanation: Nesting recovered only above an herb-cover threshold after pulling, while remaining root crowns resprouted. That supports conditional, incomplete restoration, not a cat exodus or a vine that cannot handle wet soil.

distractorExplanations.b: Cats are discussed as hunters in simplified layers, not as permanently leaving after any pull.
distractorExplanations.c: Resprouts from wet-soil crowns show the vine can persist there, not that it cannot grow.
distractorExplanations.d: The pull program was needed; the text does not show herbs winning with no removal.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-030.prompt: Researchers claim that a nightly serving of walnuts lowers fasting triglycerides, citing volunteers who already ate walnuts and had lower readings than non-eaters. Which finding, if true, most weakens the claim?

options.a: Walnuts cost more per ounce than peanuts in the grocery stores where volunteers shopped.
options.b: Walnut eaters also ran more weekly miles, a habit independently tied to lower triglycerides.
options.c: All blood draws were taken on weekday mornings for both walnut eaters and non-eaters.
options.d: Some non-eaters said they disliked the texture of walnuts and avoided them for that reason.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-030.explanation: Extra mileage is a plausible alternate cause of the triglyceride gap, so walnut eating may only mark an already-active group.

distractorExplanations.a: Price does not create the biomarker difference.
distractorExplanations.c: Weekday draws, if applied to both groups, do not explain a between-group gap.
distractorExplanations.d: Texture dislike explains avoidance, not why eaters have lower triglycerides.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-031.prompt: Coders who wear noise-canceling headsets close more tickets per week than coders who work in open sound. The CTO concludes that headsets raise output and will require them. Which finding, if true, most weakens that conclusion?

options.a: Headset batteries must be recharged twice during a long shift, interrupting some coders.
options.b: The office keeps a supply of spare headsets so that any coder can borrow one.
options.c: Headset wearers were already the team's fastest debuggers before the devices arrived.
options.d: Some clients complain that headset wearers miss quick questions asked across the room.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-031.explanation: If wearers were already faster, the ticket gap is selection, not a headset effect, so a mandate is unjustified by these numbers.

distractorExplanations.a: Charging is an inconvenience, not a confounder of the output comparison.
distractorExplanations.b: Stock on hand does not address whether headsets caused higher ticket counts.
distractorExplanations.d: Missed hallway questions is a communication cost, not evidence against a causal output gain.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-032.prompt: A city will charge drivers a daily cordon fee to enter downtown, expecting congestion to fall. Which finding, if true, most weakens that expectation?

options.a: Downtown parking meters already accept payment through a mobile app.
options.b: Buses into downtown run every twelve minutes during the morning and evening peaks.
options.c: The daily cordon fee is lower than the average price of lunch at downtown cafes.
options.d: Many peak trips are deliveries and care workers who cannot shift time or mode.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-032.explanation: If a large share of peak trips cannot switch time or mode, the fee will collect money without much traffic reduction.

distractorExplanations.a: Meter apps are orthogonal to whether trips disappear from the cordon.
distractorExplanations.b: Frequent buses would, if anything, help the fee work by offering a substitute.
distractorExplanations.c: Comparison to lunch prices does not show that inelastic trips will keep driving.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-033.prompt: Eastbridge Transit says new express buses on Route 12 will cut average door-to-door time for current Route 12 riders. Which assumption is required?

options.a: Extra walking to fewer stops will not cancel out the time saved on board.
options.b: Route 12 express buses will be painted a new color so riders can tell them apart.
options.c: Express fares will be identical to local fares when the new service launches.
options.d: Neighboring Route 14 already runs an express service in the opposite direction.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-033.explanation: Door-to-door time falls only if station-access penalties do not consume the faster ride. That net-time assumption is required.

distractorExplanations.b: Paint color does not determine door-to-door time.
distractorExplanations.c: Fare equality is a pricing choice, not required for the time claim.
distractorExplanations.d: A different route's express is unused in the Route 12 time argument.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-034.prompt: Dune Mutual raised premiums 12 percent on cottages within two miles of the tide line, citing higher storm-surge claims. Which finding, if true, most weakens the justification?

options.a: Many cottages within the two-mile band are occupied only in summer, outside the main hurricane months.
options.b: Claims rose because a few outlier mansions flooded, while typical cottages' loss rates stayed flat.
options.c: Reinsurers offered Dune Mutual a slightly lower treaty rate this year than they charged the year before.
options.d: The tide-line maps the assessor used to draw the two-mile band were last updated about a decade ago.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-034.explanation: If the average cottage's losses were flat and a few mansions drove the mean, a blanket 12 percent on all cottages is not justified by typical risk.

distractorExplanations.a: Seasonal use might cut exposure but does not show the cited claims spike is misleading.
distractorExplanations.c: A cheaper treaty would, if anything, ease pressure to raise premiums.
distractorExplanations.d: Stale maps could be a separate issue; they do not show the claims composition is skewed.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-035.prompt: Many drivers assume a higher rural speed limit must raise fatalities. After Lark State lifted the limit on two-lane roads, fatalities per mile fell slightly. Which finding, if true, most helps reconcile the result with the common assumption?

options.a: Lark State's gasoline tax rose in the same budget year that the two-lane speed limit was lifted.
options.b: Tourist brochures continued to list the old speed limit for six months after the change.
options.c: The state also added rumble strips and closed high-crash passing zones when the limit changed.
options.d: Motorcycle registrations in Lark State were nearly unchanged in the year the higher limit took effect.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-035.explanation: Engineering fixes introduced with the limit can cut deaths even if speed itself is riskier, reconciling a fatality drop with the usual speed-death link.

distractorExplanations.a: A gas-tax change does not obviously offset speed risk on two-lane roads.
distractorExplanations.b: Stale brochures would delay, not reverse, a fatality effect of the new limit.
distractorExplanations.d: Stable motorcycle counts remove one confound but do not explain a fatality drop under a higher limit.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-037.prompt: A column claims winter vitamin D capsules prevent colds because capsule users reported fewer sick days than non-users. Which finding, if true, most weakens the claim?

options.a: Capsules were sold in both 1,000- and 2,000-unit strengths, and users chose their own dose.
options.b: Many non-users said they spent most winter weekends outdoors in the sunlight.
options.c: The column appeared in a fitness magazine rather than in a peer-reviewed medical journal.
options.d: Capsule users were also more likely to work from home, away from office viruses.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-037.explanation: Work-from-home cuts exposure and can produce fewer sick days without vitamin D doing the work, undercutting the causal column.

distractorExplanations.a: Dose strength variation does not by itself create a user/non-user gap.
distractorExplanations.b: Outdoor weekends among non-users would, if anything, give non-users more vitamin D, which would not explain users' fewer sick days.
distractorExplanations.c: Venue of publication is not evidence about the causal mechanism.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-038.prompt: After Pell County replaced paper parking permits with a phone app, fine revenue fell 30 percent in year one. The treasurer says residents became more law-abiding. Which finding, if true, most weakens that explanation?

options.a: Enforcement officers spent months learning the app and issued far fewer tickets than before.
options.b: The app displays a digital clock and a countdown timer on its home screen.
options.c: Residents rated the new app as easier to use than the old paper permits.
options.d: Nearby counties that still use paper hangtags saw their parking-fine revenue stay flat that year.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-038.explanation: If ticketing effort collapsed during the learning period, revenue can fall without any rise in compliance.

distractorExplanations.b: A clock display does not explain a 30 percent revenue drop.
distractorExplanations.c: Ease of use does not separate a rise in compliance from a drop in ticketing.
distractorExplanations.d: Flat revenue in paper counties fits either explanation, so it does not weaken the treasurer's claim.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-039.prompt: A marine lab argues that warmer water, not farm runoff, caused a kelp die-off, because satellite temperatures rose in the same months kelp canopy shrank. Which finding, if true, most weakens that argument?

options.a: Kelp canopies in a warmer bay farther south shrank even more during that same season.
options.b: Runoff spiked with the heat, and a cove with the same heat but no runoff kept its kelp.
options.c: Tourist kayak rentals near the die-off site fell sharply during the same summer months.
options.d: The satellite temperature series has only a two-kilometer resolution along that stretch of coast.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-039.explanation: A same-heat, low-runoff cove that kept kelp, plus simultaneous runoff, offers a comparison that points to pollution rather than heat alone.

distractorExplanations.a: A bigger loss in warmer water fits the heat explanation, so it supports rather than weakens the lab's argument.
distractorExplanations.c: Kayak rentals are an economic side effect, not a cause of the die-off.
distractorExplanations.d: Coarser resolution is a measurement caveat, not a direct alternative cause.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-040.prompt: Since a dockless e-scooter program launched, emergency-room visits for street injuries rose 15 percent. A council member blames the scooters. Which finding, if true, most weakens that blame?

options.a: Riders must watch a short safety video before unlocking a scooter for the first time.
options.b: The city painted several miles of new protected bicycle lanes downtown during the same year.
options.c: A tourism festival and a new stadium opened that year, adding pedestrian and car traffic.
options.d: Scooter batteries are swapped overnight by contractors who ride cargo bikes between charging hubs.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-040.explanation: Extra festival and stadium traffic can lift injury visits without scooters being the driver of the 15 percent rise.

distractorExplanations.a: A safety video would, if anything, cut scooter injuries, not explain the rise.
distractorExplanations.b: New bike lanes would more likely protect cyclists than explain more ER visits.
distractorExplanations.d: Nighttime battery swaps do not account for a citywide injury-visit increase.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-041.prompt: A cafe chain finds that shops with counter tablets sell 10 percent more pastry add-ons per customer than shops with only cashiers. Managers conclude that tablets cause the extra sales. Which finding, if true, most weakens that conclusion?

options.a: Tablets sometimes freeze during the breakfast rush, forcing staff to take orders by hand.
options.b: Cashiers earn the same commission on pastry add-ons as staff in the tablet shops.
options.c: Some customers pay with cash even at counters that have tablets.
options.d: The tablet shops were already the busiest locations before the devices were installed.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-041.explanation: If tablet shops were already high-volume, the add-on gap can be location, not the interface, so the causal conclusion is unsupported.

distractorExplanations.a: Freezing would hinder, not create, extra add-on sales.
distractorExplanations.b: Equal commission removes one incentive difference but leaves the location confound untouched.
distractorExplanations.c: Cash at a tablet counter does not show that tablets fail to prompt extra pastry add-ons.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-042.prompt: E-cargo bike sales in Portmead doubled last year, yet the share of workers who commute by bicycle was unchanged. Which finding, if true, best explains the pair of facts?

options.a: Most new e-cargo bikes went to bakeries and grocers for deliveries, not to commuters.
options.b: Portmead added two miles of painted bike lanes along its waterfront path last year.
options.c: E-cargo bikes weigh considerably more than ordinary road bikes when unloaded.
options.d: A nearby city reported a small rise in weekend recreational cycling over the same year.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-042.explanation: If commercial deliveries absorbed the sales boom, commuter mode share can sit still while unit sales double.

distractorExplanations.b: New lanes would more likely raise commuter share, not hold it flat.
distractorExplanations.c: Weight is a design fact, not an explanation of who bought the extra bikes.
distractorExplanations.d: Another city's recreation trend does not account for Portmead's sales-versus-commute split.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-043.prompt: After Millford's pool offered free child lessons, reported child drownings in open water rose the next summer. Critics say the lessons failed. Which finding, if true, most helps the city reply?

options.a: The pool expanded its supervised hours into weekday evenings during the same summer.
options.b: A heat wave drew far more children to unsupervised quarries, raising their exposure.
options.c: Most children who took the free lessons lived within walking distance of the pool.
options.d: Adult lap swim at the pool stayed ticketed at the same price while child lessons became free.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-043.explanation: A heat-driven jump in quarry swimming can lift drownings even if lessons helped those who took them, so the rise does not show the program failed.

distractorExplanations.a: Longer pool hours would tend to increase supervised swim time, not explain more open-water deaths.
distractorExplanations.c: Where the learners lived does not explain why open-water drownings rose.
distractorExplanations.d: Adult lap prices do not affect child open-water exposure.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-044.prompt: Agronomists say a new three-crop rotation, not a wet spring, explains higher wheat yields in Hollow County. Which finding, if true, most strengthens that claim?

options.a: Wheat futures prices rose during the same marketing year as the higher yields.
options.b: Hollow County's extension office mailed farmers a pamphlet explaining the rotation in February.
options.c: Ridge County next door had the same wet spring, kept its old rotation, and saw no yield jump.
options.d: Some Hollow farms still plant a winter cover crop that is not part of the new rotation.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-044.explanation: A same-weather neighbor without the rotation and without the yield jump isolates rotation as the differing factor.

distractorExplanations.a: Futures prices do not identify what raised physical yields.
distractorExplanations.b: Mailing a pamphlet shows outreach, not that rotation rather than rain did the work.
distractorExplanations.d: Farms skipping the new rotation would, if anything, blur the county-wide attribution.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-045.prompt: Diggers found charred millet grains in a hearth dated 8,500 years ago and concluded the occupants farmed millet. Which finding, if true, most weakens that conclusion?

options.a: The hearth stones show repeated heating and cooling cracks from long use.
options.b: In later periods, millet straw was commonly used as bedding for livestock.
options.c: A nearby stream may have flooded the terrace where the hearth sits each spring.
options.d: The grains match a wild millet that sheds easily and was likely gathered.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-045.explanation: If the grains are morphologically wild and shatter-prone, gathering explains their presence without cultivation.

distractorExplanations.a: Heat cracks confirm a hearth, not farming.
distractorExplanations.b: Later bedding use does not speak to this 8,500-year-old deposit.
distractorExplanations.c: A possible flood is speculative and does not identify the grains as wild versus sown.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-046.prompt: To lift sales of its house-brand crackers, a grocer will move them to eye-level shelves now used by national brands. Which assumption is required?

options.a: Some shoppers who reach for eye-level crackers will pick the house brand once it sits there.
options.b: The house-brand box will be redesigned in a brighter color before it moves up to eye level.
options.c: National brands will not lower their wholesale prices in response to the move.
options.d: The grocer's warehouse already holds enough extra cases of house-brand crackers for the first month.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-046.explanation: The plan works only if eye-level placement actually switches some buyers. Without that substitution, moving boxes will not lift house-brand sales.

distractorExplanations.b: A color redesign is a separate marketing choice, not required by the shelf-height mechanism.
distractorExplanations.c: National price responses would matter for margins, not for the stated placement mechanism.
distractorExplanations.d: Warehouse stock is an operations detail, not a logical requirement of the sales argument.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-047.prompt: After Brookbend installed brighter lamps on Maple Avenue, reported night crashes on that street fell. The engineer credits the lamps. Which finding, if true, most weakens that credit?

options.a: Residents on Maple Avenue said the brighter lamps made them feel safer walking at night.
options.b: The city also retimed the Maple Avenue signals and added a crosswalk that month.
options.c: Nearby Elm Street still uses the older, dimmer fixtures along its whole length.
options.d: Some residents complained that the new lamps shine harshly into bedroom windows.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-047.explanation: Signal timing and a new crossing are independent safety changes that can cut crashes without the lamps being responsible.

distractorExplanations.a: Feeling safer is a pedestrian perception; it offers no other cause for fewer crashes.
distractorExplanations.c: Elm Street's dimmer lamps are a contrast, not a confound on Maple.
distractorExplanations.d: Bedroom glare is a nuisance complaint, not an alternative crash-reduction cause.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-048.prompt: A studio moved to a four-day on-site week. Over the next half year, client-reported defects in its apps fell. Leadership credits extra rest. Which finding, if true, most weakens that explanation?

options.a: Some staff still answered client chat messages on their weekends off.
options.b: The studio's kitchen began stocking higher-quality coffee after the schedule change.
options.c: That same week, the studio finally shipped a long-delayed automated test suite.
options.d: A rival studio kept its five-day on-site week during the same period.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-048.explanation: A new test suite can catch defects before clients see them, so the drop need not come from rest.

distractorExplanations.a: Weekend chat would cut rest, which would not explain fewer defects via the rest theory.
distractorExplanations.b: Coffee quality is a weak, unrelated alternative compared with a testing-system launch.
distractorExplanations.d: A rival's calendar does not explain this studio's defect drop.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-049.prompt: Every scooter sold by Nox Motion includes a two-year battery warranty. Some Nox scooters are sold to rental fleets. Nox's city scooters are all rental-fleet sales. Which conclusion must be true?

options.a: No privately owned Nox scooter comes with the two-year battery warranty.
options.b: Every rental-fleet scooter operating in the city is made by Nox Motion.
options.c: Nox's city scooters lack battery warranties because rental fleets self-insure.
options.d: Every Nox city scooter comes with the two-year battery warranty.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-049.explanation: City scooters are Nox rental-fleet sales, and every Nox scooter—including fleet units—has the warranty, so every city scooter has it.

distractorExplanations.a: Private sales are not shown to lack warranties; all Nox scooters have them.
distractorExplanations.b: Other brands may also sell to city fleets; the premises never close that door.
distractorExplanations.c: Self-insurance is invented; the premises assign warranties to every Nox scooter.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-050.prompt: A district says students in its new evening algebra clinic raised grades more than classmates who skipped it, so the clinic works. Which finding, if true, most weakens that inference?

options.a: Clinic joiners already scored higher, had tutors, and attended more class days.
options.b: The clinic used the same algebra textbook as the regular daytime course.
options.c: The district added late buses so clinic students could get home on time on most evenings.
options.d: Some students who skipped the clinic played a sport whose practices ended after 6 p.m.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-050.explanation: Pre-existing achievement, tutors, and attendance can produce the grade gap without the clinic causing it.

distractorExplanations.b: A shared textbook would, if anything, make the groups more comparable.
distractorExplanations.c: On-time buses are a logistics plus, not a confounder that explains skippers' weaker grades.
distractorExplanations.d: A schedule conflict explains why some students skipped, not why joiners' grades rose more.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-051.prompt: To draw more visitors under 30, a maritime museum will add touchscreen ship simulators. Which finding, if true, most weakens the plan's reasoning?

options.a: The simulators require a staff member nearby during busy weekend hours.
options.b: Young visitors come for the outdoor dry-dock, and indoor screens do not change that.
options.c: A history museum in another city attracts young visitors with audio guides instead of screens.
options.d: The simulators let visitors steer both sailing ships and steamships through historic harbors.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-051.explanation: If the under-30 audience is already coming for the dry-dock and ignores indoor screens, the simulators will not deliver the targeted attendance gain.

distractorExplanations.a: Staffing cost objects to operations, not to whether screens attract younger visitors.
distractorExplanations.c: Another museum's audio guides do not show screens will fail here.
distractorExplanations.d: Sail versus steam display range does not weaken the attendance mechanism.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-053.prompt: Researchers note that towns with more public libraries per resident have higher adult literacy, and they conclude that building libraries raises literacy. Which finding, if true, most weakens that conclusion?

options.a: Some libraries host evening knitting groups and chess clubs in their meeting rooms.
options.b: Library construction costs vary widely from town to town, depending mostly on local land prices.
options.c: Wealth and schooling independently produce both more libraries and higher literacy.
options.d: A few towns with many libraries closed one branch on Sundays last year to save on staffing.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-053.explanation: If wealth and schooling jointly generate libraries and literacy, the correlation is confounded and building libraries need not raise literacy.

distractorExplanations.a: Knitting groups are an extra use of space, not an alternative cause of the literacy correlation.
distractorExplanations.b: Land prices affect cost, not the causal reading of the correlation.
distractorExplanations.d: Sunday closures are a minor schedule change, not a confounder of the town-level pattern.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-054.prompt: In Basin Q, every orchard that grows pears also grows apples. Some apple orchards in Basin Q use frost fans. No pear orchard uses drip lines. Which conclusion must be true?

options.a: Every apple orchard in Basin Q also grows pears alongside its apple trees.
options.b: At least some of the pear orchards in Basin Q use frost fans.
options.c: Some apple orchards in Basin Q that use frost fans also grow pears.
options.d: No orchard in Basin Q that grows both pears and apples uses drip lines.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-054.explanation: The last premise already states that no pear orchard uses drip lines. Pear-and-apple orchards are still pear orchards, so they too lack drip lines. The other options reverse or overreach the some/every statements.

distractorExplanations.a: Pears imply apples, not the reverse; apple-only orchards may exist.
distractorExplanations.b: Fans on some apple orchards need not include any pear orchard.
distractorExplanations.c: Fans are on some apple orchards, but nothing says any of those orchards grow pears.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-056.prompt: Some managers say remote work wrecks culture because people rarely share a kitchen. A critic replies that culture is mainly shared standards for decisions, which can be taught in writing. Which option most accurately describes the critic's technique?

options.a: The critic redefines culture so that physical proximity is no longer essential to it.
options.b: The critic cites evidence that remote teams report higher job satisfaction than office teams.
options.c: The critic argues that maintaining office kitchens costs more than collaboration software.
options.d: The critic claims that remote employees produce more measured output per hour than office staff.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-056.explanation: Managers treat kitchen contact as culture; the critic substitutes decision standards that do not require a kitchen, which is a definitional shift.

distractorExplanations.b: No satisfaction evidence appears; the critic changes what culture means.
distractorExplanations.c: Cost of kitchens versus software is not the critic's move.
distractorExplanations.d: Output per hour is a productivity claim the critic does not make.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-057.prompt: HR notes that staff who attend optional posture workshops take fewer sick days and concludes the workshops cut illness. Which finding, if true, most weakens that conclusion?

options.a: Workshop attendees rated the sessions highly and asked HR to schedule a second series.
options.b: Attendees were already more health-conscious and took fewer sick days before the series.
options.c: The workshops were scheduled during lunch hours so that no one had to miss work to attend.
options.d: HR plans to make the posture workshops mandatory for all staff next year.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-057.explanation: A pre-existing health gap means workshops may only attract people who were going to be well anyway.

distractorExplanations.a: Liking the workshops does not show that they cause fewer sick days.
distractorExplanations.c: Convenient scheduling does not bear on whether attendance causes fewer sick days.
distractorExplanations.d: A future plan is not evidence about the past link between attendance and sick days.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-058.prompt: An online poll on a trail-running forum found that 82 percent of respondents support a new riverside path. Advocates cite the poll as proof of citywide support. Which criticism is most to the point?

options.a: The poll asked respondents to rate several other proposed projects on a 1-to-5 scale.
options.b: Some respondents added free-text comments explaining why they supported the path.
options.c: Forum members are path enthusiasts, so the poll overrepresents supporters.
options.d: The riverside path would need new lighting and patrols if it stayed open after dusk.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-058.explanation: A self-selected enthusiast forum is not a city sample; citing 82 percent as citywide support is a biased-sample error.

distractorExplanations.a: A scale on another item does not create the sampling problem.
distractorExplanations.b: Free-text comments do not make the sample representative.
distractorExplanations.d: Lighting is a design issue, not a critique of the poll's representativeness.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-059.prompt: A mayor says 75 percent of office complaints last year were about overflowing bins, so bins are residents' biggest problem. Which option most accurately describes a flaw?

options.a: It assumes that bins overflow mostly during summer heat waves rather than throughout the year.
options.b: It fails to report how many public bins the city owns and how often crews empty them.
options.c: It assumes that fixing overflowing bins would cost the city more than repairing potholes.
options.d: It treats complaint volume as importance, though some serious harms are rarely reported.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-059.explanation: Complaint share can reflect ease of reporting, not ranking of harms. The mayor treats the 75 percent as a welfare ranking without that link.

distractorExplanations.a: Seasonality of overflow is not the mayor's stated leap.
distractorExplanations.b: Inventory of bins is unused in the importance inference.
distractorExplanations.c: Repair cost is not the argument's measure; complaint counts are.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-060.prompt: A reviewer says a poet's new collection sold fewer copies than her debut, so her craft has declined. Which criticism is most to the point?

options.a: The debut's novelty may have faded or the market shrunk, which says nothing about the poems.
options.b: The reviewer quotes only a single stanza from the new collection to illustrate the decline.
options.c: Poetry collections rarely appear on national bestseller lists, even when critics praise them.
options.d: The reviewer has praised other poets whose newer books also sold fewer copies than their debuts.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-060.explanation: The argument infers quality from units sold. Alternative commercial explanations sever that inference without denying a sales drop.

distractorExplanations.b: Quoting one stanza is a review-style complaint, not the core sales-to-quality flaw.
distractorExplanations.c: Bestseller rarity does not specifically explain this author's drop.
distractorExplanations.d: The reviewer's treatment of other poets does not address the leap from sales to craft.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-061.prompt: When a regional carrier cut fares 18 percent, total ticket revenue rose even though it added no flights. Which finding, if true, most helps explain the revenue rise?

options.a: The carrier kept its in-flight snack and coffee service unchanged after cutting fares.
options.b: Lower fares filled many empty seats, and extra passengers outweighed the price cut.
options.c: Rival carriers matched the fare cut on most of the same routes within a month.
options.d: The carrier's pilots signed a new multiyear contract earlier that year with modest raises.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-061.explanation: Revenue is price times quantity. Filling empty seats can raise the product even when price falls, which fits no added flights.

distractorExplanations.a: Coffee service does not explain a revenue jump after a fare cut.
distractorExplanations.c: Rivals matching the cut would make extra passengers less likely, so it deepens rather than explains the puzzle.
distractorExplanations.d: A pilot contract affects costs, not the fare-to-revenue arithmetic.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-062.prompt: All of this summer's interns at Helix Bio are biochemistry majors. Some of the interns received travel grants. No chemistry-department faculty member received a travel grant. Which conclusion must be true?

options.a: Every biochemistry major who works at Helix Bio this summer is one of the interns.
options.b: Some chemistry-department faculty members at Helix Bio are also biochemistry majors.
options.c: None of the travel-grant interns is a chemistry-department faculty member.
options.d: Every travel grant awarded at Helix Bio this summer went to a biochemistry major.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-062.explanation: Grant-holding interns are biochemistry majors and interns; faculty got no grants. Therefore no grant intern is a chemistry faculty member. The other choices reverse or expand the premises.

distractorExplanations.a: Interns are biochemistry majors, not the reverse.
distractorExplanations.b: Nothing in the premises shows chemistry faculty overlapping with biochemistry majors.
distractorExplanations.d: Grants to people outside the intern pool are not ruled out.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-063.prompt: Hospital North posts a higher death rate among surgical patients than Hospital South, yet surgeons still call North the stronger trauma center. Which finding, if true, most helps reconcile the two claims?

options.a: Hospital North's patient-satisfaction surveys rate its meals and rooms higher than Hospital South's surveys do.
options.b: Hospital South's surgeons publish more research papers each year than Hospital North's surgeons publish.
options.c: Hospital North charges higher fees for most surgical procedures than Hospital South charges for the same work.
options.d: North receives far more unstable transfers from other hospitals, so its surgical patients arrive much sicker.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-063.explanation: A far sicker incoming mix can raise a capable trauma center's raw death rate. If North takes most unstable transfers, its higher crude rate is compatible with surgeons judging it the stronger center, which reconciles the two claims.

distractorExplanations.a: Satisfaction with meals and rooms says nothing about surgical risk or skill, so North's higher death rate is left unexplained.
distractorExplanations.b: More research output at South, if anything, supports South's reputation, so it deepens rather than resolves the conflict with surgeons' view.
distractorExplanations.c: Higher fees at North describe pricing, not patient severity or outcomes, so they cannot explain why the stronger center has more deaths.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-064.prompt: A village replaced all-night street lamps with motion-triggered LEDs, and the lighting electricity bill fell 40 percent. Officials credit the sensors. Which finding, if true, most weakens that credit?

options.a: The village also cut the nightly hours of two floodlit sports fields that billing period.
options.b: LED bulbs last several years longer than the sodium lamps they replaced on the same poles.
options.c: A neighboring village still uses all-night sodium street lamps on its main roads.
options.d: Residents report that the motion-triggered lamps light up quickly when someone walks past.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-064.explanation: Losing sports-field flood hours can crash the lighting bill without the street sensors doing the work.

distractorExplanations.b: Longer bulb life affects replacement cost, not this period's electricity bill as directly as field hours.
distractorExplanations.c: A neighbor's old lamps do not explain this village's bill drop.
distractorExplanations.d: Quick response describes how the sensors work; it offers no other cause for the lower bill.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-065.prompt: To cut cashier turnover, Northgate Mart will raise starting pay 8 percent. Exit interviews say most leavers complained about unpredictable schedules, not pay. Which finding, if true, most weakens the raise-as-solution plan?

options.a: A rival grocer across town already pays its new cashiers a few cents more per hour.
options.b: Leavers who cited schedules would have stayed for stable hours even without a raise.
options.c: Northgate's cashier training videos are due for an update next quarter.
options.d: Northgate's cashiers rated their store managers favorably in last year's staff survey.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-065.explanation: If the binding complaint is hours, and people would stay for stable rosters without more pay, the raise will not hit the stated turnover cause.

distractorExplanations.a: A rival's wage is a market fact, not evidence that schedules—not pay—drive exits.
distractorExplanations.c: Training videos are unrelated to the exit-interview diagnosis.
distractorExplanations.d: Favorable manager ratings do not address whether pay or schedules drive cashier exits.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-066.prompt: Supporters of a checkout-bag fee in Redhill say it will cut plastic litter in creeks. Which finding, if true, most weakens that prediction?

options.a: The fee will be collected by cashiers at checkout rather than by self-service kiosks.
options.b: Redhill already recycles cardboard and glass at two municipal depots near the creeks.
options.c: Shoppers will switch to thicker plastic bags that are discarded after a few trips.
options.d: A neighboring town that adopted a similar fee prints the amount on every receipt.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-066.explanation: If the substitute is still short-lived plastic, creek litter need not fall, which undercuts the supporters' environmental prediction.

distractorExplanations.a: Who collects the fee does not determine litter outcomes.
distractorExplanations.b: Cardboard depots do not speak to plastic bag litter in creeks.
distractorExplanations.d: Receipt printing in another town is irrelevant to Redhill's litter path.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-067.prompt: A textbook house plans to lift profit by selling only digital editions, since file distribution is cheaper than printing. Which assumption is required?

options.a: Most students prefer highlighting passages on a screen to writing notes in paper margins.
options.b: Campus bookstores will keep featuring the publisher's titles in their front windows.
options.c: The publisher will cut each title's list price by the full amount saved on printing.
options.d: Sales lost to students who refuse screens will not exceed the printing savings.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-067.explanation: Profit rises only if print-cost savings outrun revenue lost from print-only buyers. That net-profit assumption is required.

distractorExplanations.a: Highlighting preference is not required for the cost-saving profit story.
distractorExplanations.b: Bookstore window display is a marketing extra, not a necessary premise.
distractorExplanations.c: Passing savings into list price would reduce, not secure, the profit claim.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-065-du.prompt: Over four years, average exam scores at Cedar Ridge High rose. The principal credits a new advisory period. Which finding, if true, most weakens that credit?

options.a: The district adopted an easier exam form and a gentler grading curve in those years.
options.b: Advisory groups meet in homerooms rather than in the gym, so no class time was lost.
options.c: Some teachers assign extra weekend reading during the weeks that advisory sessions meet.
options.d: Teachers at Cedar Ridge say students enjoy the advisory period more than study hall.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-065-du.explanation: An easier exam and a gentler curve can lift reported scores without advisory periods causing more learning.

distractorExplanations.b: Meeting room choice does not explain a four-year score rise.
distractorExplanations.c: Weekend reading would, if anything, add work, not an alternative inflation of scores.
distractorExplanations.d: Student enjoyment is not evidence about what raised the exam scores.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-066-du.prompt: Registered voters in Hillford rose 9 percent between two elections, yet votes cast fell. Which finding, if true, most helps explain the pair?

options.a: Hillford printed extra ballots for the second election in case a recount was needed.
options.b: The drive signed up people who never meant to vote, while loyal voters moved away.
options.c: Polling places in Hillford stayed open until 8 p.m. in both elections.
options.d: Turnout also fell in several neighboring towns that ran no registration drives.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-066-du.explanation: Adding non-voting registrants while losing actual voters can raise the roll and cut ballots cast at the same time.

distractorExplanations.a: Extra printed ballots are unused inventory, not an explanation of turnout.
distractorExplanations.c: Unchanged poll hours do not split registration from votes.
distractorExplanations.d: A regional turnout dip explains fewer votes but not why Hillford's registrations rose 9 percent.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-067-du.prompt: An economist says a weaker currency should lift a country's trade balance because exports cheapen for foreigners. After the currency fell, the trade balance worsened. Which finding, if true, most helps explain the surprise?

options.a: Exporters advertised their newly lower foreign-currency prices heavily across their main overseas markets.
options.b: The central bank had announced weeks in advance that it expected the currency to weaken during that quarter.
options.c: Most exporters rely on imported parts billed in foreign currency, so their production costs rose with the drop.
options.d: Residents took more domestic holidays instead of trips abroad, since foreign travel had become pricier for them.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-verbal-067-du.explanation: The economist assumes depreciation makes exports cheaper for foreigners. If exporters' imported parts are billed in foreign currency, their costs rise as the currency falls, so export prices need not drop while the import bill grows. That explains why the trade balance worsened.

distractorExplanations.a: Heavier marketing of cheaper exports should raise export volume, which deepens the puzzle instead of explaining why the balance got worse.
distractorExplanations.b: Announcing the expected drop in advance changes nothing about export costs or import bills, so it cannot explain the balance moving the wrong way.
distractorExplanations.d: Fewer trips abroad cut spending on foreign services, which pushes the balance toward improvement and makes the worsening harder to explain.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-031.prompt: What is the value of 4n − 1? Statement (1): n = 6. Statement (2): n is a positive even integer less than 20.

options.a: Statement (1) alone is sufficient, but statement (2) is not.
options.b: Statement (2) alone is sufficient, but statement (1) is not.
options.c: Both together are sufficient, but neither statement is alone.
options.d: Even combined, the two statements do not settle the question.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-031.explanation: Statement (1) pins n at 6, so 4n − 1 equals 23 with no other possibility. Statement (2) still allows n = 2, 4, 8, …, 18, each giving a different value of 4n − 1, so it cannot name a unique number on its own.

distractorExplanations.b: Statement (2) lists many even integers below 20, not a single n, so 4n − 1 is not unique from (2) alone.
distractorExplanations.c: Statement (1) already yields a unique value; pairing the statements is unnecessary.
distractorExplanations.d: A unique value is available from statement (1) alone, so the pair is not jointly insufficient.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-032.prompt: Is real number u strictly negative? Statement (1): u² = 49. Statement (2): u³ = −343.

options.a: Statement (1) alone is sufficient, but statement (2) is not.
options.b: Statement (2) alone is sufficient, but statement (1) is not.
options.c: Both together are sufficient, but neither statement is alone.
options.d: Even combined, the two statements do not settle the question.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-032.explanation: Squares hide sign: u² = 49 allows u = 7 or u = −7, so (1) cannot answer whether u is negative. Cubes keep sign: the unique real cube root of −343 is u = −7, which answers the yes/no with a definite yes. A definite yes is sufficient, so (2) alone suffices.

distractorExplanations.a: u² = 49 is compatible with both +7 and −7, so (1) leaves the sign open.
distractorExplanations.c: Statement (2) already answers the sign question; both statements are not required.
distractorExplanations.d: The real cube root of −343 is unique and negative, so the question is settled by (2).

gmat-focus-readiness-check-033.prompt: Is integer m a multiple of 12? Statement (1): m is a multiple of 4. Statement (2): m is a multiple of 6.

options.a: Statement (1) alone is sufficient, but statement (2) is not.
options.b: Statement (2) alone is sufficient, but statement (1) is not.
options.c: Both together are sufficient, but neither statement is alone.
options.d: Even combined, the two statements do not settle the question.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-033.explanation: Multiples of 4 include 4, 8, and 16, which are not all multiples of 12, so (1) is insufficient. Multiples of 6 include 6 and 18, not all multiples of 12, so (2) is insufficient. Together, m is a common multiple of 4 and 6, hence a multiple of lcm(4,6)=12, which answers yes.

distractorExplanations.a: Being a multiple of 4 does not force a factor of 3, so m need not be a multiple of 12.
distractorExplanations.b: Being a multiple of 6 does not force a factor of 4; 18 is a counterexample.
distractorExplanations.d: lcm(4,6)=12, so the two divisibility facts together do settle the question.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-034.prompt: What is the integer value of k? Statement (1): k is a prime number between 10 and 30. Statement (2): k is odd.

options.a: Statement (1) alone is sufficient, but statement (2) is not.
options.b: Statement (2) alone is sufficient, but statement (1) is not.
options.c: Both together are sufficient, but neither statement is alone.
options.d: Even combined, the two statements do not settle the question.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-034.explanation: Primes between 10 and 30 include 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, and 29. Statement (2) only notes oddness, which all of those primes already have. Even combined, several odd primes remain, so k is not unique.

distractorExplanations.a: Several primes sit between 10 and 30, so (1) does not name a unique k.
distractorExplanations.b: Oddness alone allows infinitely many integers, not a unique k.
distractorExplanations.c: Intersecting the two lists still leaves 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, and 29.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-035.prompt: If p and q are integers, is the product pq even? Statement (1): p is even. Statement (2): q is odd.

options.a: Statement (1) alone is sufficient, but statement (2) is not.
options.b: Statement (2) alone is sufficient, but statement (1) is not.
options.c: Both together are sufficient, but neither statement is alone.
options.d: Even combined, the two statements do not settle the question.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-035.explanation: An even integer times any integer is even, so (1) alone answers yes regardless of q. Statement (2) leaves p free: if p is even the product is even; if p is odd the product is odd. Only (1) is sufficient.

distractorExplanations.b: Knowing only that q is odd leaves p’s parity open, so pq may be even or odd.
distractorExplanations.c: Statement (1) already settles the product’s parity; (2) is not needed.
distractorExplanations.d: Because (1) alone answers the question, the pair is not jointly insufficient.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-036.prompt: A harbor weighed inbound recyclables in tons: glass 12, mixed paper 18, PET plastic 9, scrap metal 6. Which material is exactly 20% of the 45-ton total?

options.a: Glass, because 12 tons is a frequent inbound stream
options.b: PET plastic, because 9 of 45 tons is exactly one-fifth
options.c: Mixed paper, because it is the largest inbound tonnage
options.d: Scrap metal, because six tons is the smallest inbound load

gmat-focus-readiness-check-036.explanation: The total is 12+18+9+6=45 tons. PET plastic is 9/45=0.20, so it is exactly one-fifth. Glass is 12/45≈26.7%, paper 40%, metal 13.3%. Share, not rank, is what the item asks.

distractorExplanations.a: Glass’s 12 tons is about 26.7% of 45, not 20%; stream frequency is not the share.
distractorExplanations.c: Largest tonnage (paper at 40%) is not the 20% share requested.
distractorExplanations.d: Smallest load (metal) is about 13.3% of the total, not 20%.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-037.prompt: Trail-mix labels list calories and protein per pouch: Cedar 210 kcal / 6 g; Pine 180 / 9; Maple 240 / 8; Birch 150 / 5. Which pouch has the most protein per 100 kcal?

options.a: Cedar, because 210 calories is a midrange pouch size
options.b: Maple, because 8 grams is the second-highest protein
options.c: Pine, because 9 g on 180 kcal is 5.0 g per 100 kcal
options.d: Birch, because 150 calories is the lightest pouch listed

gmat-focus-readiness-check-037.explanation: Protein per 100 kcal: Cedar 6/2.10≈2.86; Pine 9/1.80=5.00; Maple 8/2.40≈3.33; Birch 5/1.50≈3.33. Pine is highest. Comparing raw grams or calories alone misses the density ratio.

distractorExplanations.a: Cedar’s calorie count does not make it densest; 6 g / 210 kcal is only about 2.86 per 100 kcal.
distractorExplanations.b: Maple’s 8 g is not the top protein, and 8/240 kcal is about 3.33 per 100 kcal, below Pine.
distractorExplanations.d: Lightest pouch is not densest; Birch is about 3.33 g per 100 kcal, below Pine.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-039.prompt: Four hospital units report headcount and mean annual pay: ICU 12 staff × $92k; Ward 40 × $58k; Lab 8 × $71k; Transport 15 × $44k. Which unit has the largest payroll?

options.a: ICU
options.b: Lab
options.c: Transport
options.d: Ward

gmat-focus-readiness-check-039.explanation: Payroll = headcount × mean pay: ICU 12×92k=$1.104M; Ward 40×58k=$2.32M; Lab 8×71k=$0.568M; Transport 15×44k=$0.66M. The Ward’s large roster outweighs its lower mean.

distractorExplanations.a: ICU has the highest mean pay, but 12 × $92k = $1.104M, less than half the Ward's $2.32M; a high average on a small roster loses to headcount.
distractorExplanations.b: Lab's 8 × $71k = $0.568M is the smallest payroll of the four; a mid-range mean cannot offset the smallest roster.
distractorExplanations.c: Transport's 15 × $44k = $0.66M; a bigger roster than ICU cannot make up for the lowest mean pay in the table.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-040.prompt: A museum’s monthly web visits (thousands) were Jan 40, Feb 44, Mar 48, Apr 42, May 46. From January to March the series is linear. Which statement is accurate?

options.a: Visits rose 4,000 per month Jan–Mar, then fell 6,000 in April
options.b: April traffic was the peak month across the whole five-month window
options.c: May visits were 20% below the January starting count shown
options.d: The five monthly readings sum to fewer than 200,000 visits

gmat-focus-readiness-check-040.explanation: Jan→Feb→Mar: 40, 44, 48 is a constant +4 (thousand) slope, i.e. +4,000 visits per month. April 42 is 6 thousand below March 48. May 46 is not the peak; the five months total 220 thousand.

distractorExplanations.b: April 42k is a dip, not the peak; March 48k is the highest reading.
distractorExplanations.c: May 46k is above January 40k, not 20% below it.
distractorExplanations.d: The five months total 220 thousand visits, which exceeds 200,000.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-041.prompt: A café logged complaint tickets by week: W1 8, W2 12, W3 10, W4 14. Relative to week 1, by what percent did week 4 tickets change?

options.a: A 50% increase, because 12 is 4 more than 8, and 4/8 = 0.5
options.b: A 75% increase, because 14 is 6 more than 8, and 6/8 = 0.75
options.c: A 75% decrease, because tickets fell back after the second week
options.d: No net change, because weeks 2 and 3 average back to 8

gmat-focus-readiness-check-041.explanation: Percent change uses (new − old)/old. (14 − 8)/8 = 6/8 = 0.75, a 75% increase. A 50% rise from 8 would be +4 to 12, but week 4 is 14. Week 3’s dip does not reverse the W1-to-W4 comparison.

distractorExplanations.a: Uses week 2 (12) as the new value; week 4 is 14, which is 6 above week 1.
distractorExplanations.c: Week 4 is higher than week 1, so the W1-to-W4 change is an increase.
distractorExplanations.d: Weeks 2–3 averaging 11 does not cancel the rise from 8 to 14.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-042.prompt: A tutoring app’s monthly active users (thousands) were M1 20, M2 24, M3 30, M4 28, M5 35. Which two-part reading of growth is correct?

options.a: M1→M2 grew 20% and M4 was the five-month peak
options.b: M2→M3 grew 10% and users never declined in any month
options.c: M1→M2 grew 20% and M3→M4 was the only month-to-month drop
options.d: M4→M5 grew 10% and the series is strictly increasing throughout

gmat-focus-readiness-check-042.explanation: (24−20)/20=20% from M1 to M2. The only decline is 30→28 from M3 to M4. M5 35 is the peak. M2→M3 is (30−24)/24=25%, not 10%. M4→M5 is (35−28)/28=25%, not 10%.

distractorExplanations.a: The 20% M1→M2 rise is right, but M4 28k is not the peak; M5 is 35k.
distractorExplanations.b: M2→M3 is a 25% rise, not 10%, and M3→M4 is a decline.
distractorExplanations.d: M4→M5 is about 25%, not 10%, and M3→M4 breaks a strictly increasing path.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-043.prompt: Source A (bonus memo): “A year-end bonus is paid only if the employee’s year-end rating is at least 4.0 and paid overtime hours for the year exceed 40.” Source B (roster): Jordan rating 4.2, overtime 38; Riley 3.9, overtime 55; Avery 4.0, overtime 40; Quinn 4.5, overtime 41. Who is eligible under both rules as written?

options.a: Jordan, because a 4.2 rating clears the quality threshold
options.b: Riley, because 55 overtime hours is the roster’s maximum
options.c: Avery, because a 4.0 rating and 40 hours each meet a cutoff
options.d: Quinn, because 4.5 exceeds 4.0 and 41 hours exceed 40

gmat-focus-readiness-check-043.explanation: The memo uses “at least 4.0” and “exceed 40.” Avery’s 40 hours do not exceed 40. Jordan’s 38 hours fail overtime. Riley’s 3.9 fails the rating. Only Quinn satisfies both: 4.5 ≥ 4.0 and 41 > 40.

distractorExplanations.a: Jordan’s rating is high enough, but 38 overtime hours do not exceed 40.
distractorExplanations.b: Riley’s overtime is high, but a 3.9 rating is below the 4.0 floor.
distractorExplanations.c: Avery’s 40 hours fail “exceed 40”; equality is not enough on that clause.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-044.prompt: Source 1 (fulfillment rule): “Free ground shipping if the merchandise subtotal is over $50; two-day shipping is $12 unless the subtotal is over $90, in which case two-day is $4.” Source 2 (cart): knit hat $18, field guide $28, rain cover $16. A shopper wants two-day delivery. What shipping charge applies?

options.a: Twelve dollars, because $62 is over $50 but not over $90
options.b: Four dollars, because any three-item cart gets the $4 two-day rate
options.c: Zero dollars, because a cart over $50 always ships two-day free
options.d: Sixteen dollars for two-day delivery on the $62 cart

gmat-focus-readiness-check-044.explanation: Subtotal 18+28+16=$62. Ground would be free (> $50), but the shopper chose two-day. Two-day is $12 unless the subtotal is over $90; $62 is not, so the charge is $12.

distractorExplanations.b: The $4 two-day rate requires a subtotal over $90, not merely three line items.
distractorExplanations.c: Over-$50 free shipping is for ground only; two-day remains a paid option here.
distractorExplanations.d: The $12 and $4 amounts are alternative rates, not fees to add together.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-045.prompt: Source 1: “Flight 811 leaves Harbor City at 09:15 and is wheels-down in Mesa at 11:05 same clock time (no zone change). Minimum connection is 40 minutes.” Source 2: “Flight 920, the only Mesa→Ridge afternoon option, boards at 11:30 and pushes at 11:50.” Can a passenger on 811 make 920 the same day?

options.a: Yes, because 11:05 to 11:50 is a 45-minute window on the clock
options.b: No, because 11:05 to 11:30 boarding is only 25 minutes
options.c: Yes, because same-clock cities ignore the 40-minute connection rule
options.d: No, because Flight 920 is described as a morning departure from Mesa

gmat-focus-readiness-check-045.explanation: Arrival 11:05 versus board 11:30 is 25 minutes, short of the 40-minute minimum. Same local clocks do not waive the connection buffer. 11:50 push is afternoon, not morning.

distractorExplanations.a: The relevant cut is boarding at 11:30, not push at 11:50; 11:05→11:30 is 25 minutes.
distractorExplanations.c: No zone change does not cancel the stated 40-minute minimum connection.
distractorExplanations.d: Source 2 places 920 in the afternoon (11:50 push), not the morning.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A ceramics kiln logs defect counts on 200-piece lots: glaze pits 14, hairline cracks 9, warping 5, stain 2. What share of all 30 defects is warping?
gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Defects total 14+9+5+2=30. Warping is 5/30=1/6. The 200-piece lot size is the production base, not the defect denominator unless the question asks defect rate per piece.

distractorExplanations.a: 5/200 is warping per piece in the lot, a defect rate; the question asks for warping's share of the 30 recorded defects.
distractorExplanations.c: 5/28 leaves the 2 stain defects out of the total; the question asks for the share of all 30 defects, so the denominator is 30.
distractorExplanations.d: 3/10 is 9/30, the hairline-crack share; warping accounts for 5 of the 30 defects, which is 1/6.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A ranger recorded five trail lengths in km but the notebook page is smudged. What is the median length? Statement (1): The longest trail is 15 km. Statement (2): The shortest trail is 7 km.

options.a: Statement (1) alone is sufficient, but statement (2) is not.
options.b: Statement (2) alone is sufficient, but statement (1) is not.
options.c: Both together are sufficient, but neither statement is alone.
options.d: Even combined, the two statements do not settle the question.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: For five numbers the median is the third when ordered. Statement (1) only caps the largest; statement (2) only floors the smallest. Even together, many triples can sit between 7 and 15, so the third value is not unique.

distractorExplanations.a: Knowing only the longest trail does not identify the ordered third length.
distractorExplanations.b: Knowing only the shortest trail leaves every other length, including the median, open.
distractorExplanations.c: A min of 7 and a max of 15 still allow many different middle values.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Headcount by department: Sales 40, Ops 25, Finance 15, Design 20. Which department is 25% of the 100-person firm?

options.a: Ops, because 25 of 100 employees is exactly one-quarter
options.b: Sales, because 40 people is the largest department listed
options.c: Finance, because 15 people is the smallest department listed
options.d: Design, because 20 of the 100 employees is one-quarter

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Total 40+25+15+20=100. Ops 25/100=25%. Sales is 40%, Design 20%, Finance 15%. One-fifth is 20%, not 25%.

distractorExplanations.b: Largest share (Sales at 40%) is not the 25% share asked.
distractorExplanations.c: Smallest share (Finance at 15%) is not 25%.
distractorExplanations.d: Design is 20% (one-fifth), which is not 25%.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A clinic’s annual visits (thousands) follow V(t)=3t+18 for t = years after 2020. Which pair is correct for 2022 (t=2) and the implied 2020 starting level?

options.a: 2022 visits 24 thousand; 2020 starting level 3 thousand
options.b: 2022 visits 24 thousand; 2020 starting level 18 thousand
options.c: 2022 visits 21 thousand; 2020 starting level 18 thousand
options.d: 2022 visits 36 thousand; 2020 starting level 21 thousand

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: V(2)=3(2)+18=24. The intercept V(0)=18 is the 2020 level. 3 is the annual slope in thousands, not the intercept. 3t+18 at t=2 is not 21 or 36.

distractorExplanations.a: 24 thousand for 2022 is right, but 3 is the slope, not the 2020 intercept.
distractorExplanations.c: 18 thousand is the 2020 intercept, but V(2)=24, not 21.
distractorExplanations.d: 36 would be 18×2, which ignores the actual 3t+18 arithmetic.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Bottles filled per hour: Line K 40, 36, 44, 40; Line L 38, 42, 41, 39. Which comparison of four-hour means is right?

options.a: Line K’s mean is 44, matching its best hour
options.b: Line L’s mean is 38, matching its weakest hour
options.c: Both lines average 40 bottles per hour
options.d: Line L averages 4 bottles per hour more than Line K

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: K: (40+36+44+40)/4=160/4=40. L: (38+42+41+39)/4=160/4=40. Means match. Using a single best or worst hour as the mean is the trap.

distractorExplanations.a: 44 is K’s peak hour, not the four-hour mean of 40.
distractorExplanations.b: 38 is L’s weakest hour, not its mean of 40.
distractorExplanations.d: The two means are equal at 40, so L is not 4 bottles ahead.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Two regions’ shares (%) t years after a launch: North = 8 + 2t, South = 20 − t. After how many years are the shares equal, and what is that common share?

options.a: Equal after 4 years at a 20% share each
options.b: Equal after 6 years at an 8% share each
options.c: Equal after 12 years at a 2% share each
options.d: Equal after 4 years at a 16% share each

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Set 8+2t = 20−t → 3t=12 → t=4. Then North = 8+8=16 and South=20−4=16. Four years at 20% would treat South’s intercept as the meeting height.

distractorExplanations.a: t=4 is correct, but the common share is 16%, not South’s starting 20%.
distractorExplanations.b: t=6 is not the solution of 8+2t=20−t; 8% is North’s intercept, not the crossing.
distractorExplanations.c: t=12 would follow if 2t=12 were used without moving −t; 2% is a coefficient, not the share.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Source A (returns desk): “A full refund issues only if the tag is intact and the return is within 14 days of the invoice date.” Source B: invoice 3 June; return 16 June; tag intact. The desk counts the invoice day as day 0. Is a full refund due?

options.a: Yes: 13 days have elapsed, and the tag is intact
options.b: No: counting 3 June as day 1 puts the return past the window
options.c: No: a full refund also requires the original receipt
options.d: Partly: only store credit is due after 10 days

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Day 0 is 3 June, so 16 June is day 13, within the 14-day window, and the tag is intact. Both of Source A's conditions hold, so a full refund is due. Receipt or 10-day rules appear in neither source.

distractorExplanations.b: Even counting 3 June as day 1 gives 14 days, still within 14; and the desk counts the invoice day as day 0, which gives 13.
distractorExplanations.c: Source A lists only two conditions, an intact tag and the 14-day window; a receipt rule appears in neither source.
distractorExplanations.d: No 10-day cutoff or store-credit rule appears in Source A; 13 days is inside the 14-day full-refund window.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A community choir’s 200 seats split as student 50%, adult 30%, senior 20%. How many seats are adult or senior?

options.a: 40 seats
options.b: 60 seats
options.c: 100 seats
options.d: 150 seats

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Adult or senior is 30%+20%=50% of 200 = 100. Students are a separate slice. Taking only adult or only senior undercounts the union of those two disjoint slices.

distractorExplanations.a: 40 is seniors alone and omits the adult slice.
distractorExplanations.b: 60 is adults alone; seniors must be included in “adult or senior.”
distractorExplanations.d: 150 adds students to adults and omits the requested senior group.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Grant dollars (thousands) follow G(t)=t² + 4t + 5, t = years after the seed year. What is G(3), and how much did G rise from t=2 to t=3?

options.a: G(3)=26 and the rise from t=2 is 4 thousand
options.b: G(3)=17 and the rise from t=2 is 9 thousand
options.c: G(3)=26 and the rise from t=2 is 9 thousand
options.d: G(3)=32 and the rise from t=2 is 5 thousand

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: G(3)=9+12+5=26. G(2)=4+8+5=17. Rise = 26−17=9. The linear 4t term is not the year-3 increment. 32 would mix t² and 4t incorrectly.

distractorExplanations.a: G(3)=26 is right, but the increment from 17 is 9, not the coefficient 4.
distractorExplanations.b: The rise 9 is right (26−17), but G(3) is 26, not 17; 17 is G(2).
distractorExplanations.d: 32 is not G(3); 5 is the constant term, not the t=2-to-3 change.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Source 1: “Promotion requires 24 months in grade and a completed leadership clinic.” Source 2 roster: Sam 26 months, clinic incomplete; Pat 24 months, clinic complete; Chris 18 months, clinic complete; Dana 30 months, clinic complete but on a performance warning the memo never mentions. Who meets the two written requirements?

options.a: Sam only, because 26 months is the longest tenure shown
options.b: Chris only, because finishing the clinic overrides short tenure
options.c: Sam and Dana, because both exceed 24 months in grade
options.d: Pat and Dana, because each has ≥24 months and the clinic done

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Both listed gates are tenure ≥24 months and clinic complete. Pat (24, complete) and Dana (30, complete) meet them. Sam lacks the clinic. Chris has only 18 months. A warning not mentioned in Source 1 is outside the written test.

distractorExplanations.a: Sam’s tenure is enough, but the incomplete clinic fails Source 1.
distractorExplanations.b: Chris’s clinic is complete, but 18 months is below the 24-month gate.
distractorExplanations.c: Sam still lacks the clinic; tenure alone does not promote.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Four-month output (crates): Mill P 80, 90, 70, 100; Mill Q 95, 85, 90, 90. Which mill has the larger four-month total, and by how many crates?

options.a: Q by 20 crates: 360 versus P’s 340
options.b: P by 20 crates: 360 versus Q’s 340
options.c: Q by 5 crates: 350 versus P’s 345
options.d: The mills tie at 360 crates over the four months

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: P: 80+90+70+100=340. Q: 95+85+90+90=360. Q leads by 20. Swapping who has 360 is the main arithmetic trap. A tie ignores the 20-crate gap.

distractorExplanations.b: P totals 340, not 360; swapping the mills reverses the leader.
distractorExplanations.c: Neither 350 nor 345 matches the actual 360 vs 340 totals.
distractorExplanations.d: The totals differ by 20 crates; they are not tied.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Relay boards tested: Type F 50 units, 4 defects; Type G 80, 10; Type H 40, 2; Type J 30, 6. Which type has the highest defect rate?

options.a: Type G, because 10 defects is the largest defect count
options.b: Type J, because 6 defects in 30 units is a 20% rate
options.c: Type F, because 50 units is a mid-size production lot
options.d: Type H, because 2 defects is the smallest defect count

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Rates: F 4/50=8%; G 10/80=12.5%; H 2/40=5%; J 6/30=20%. Highest rate is J. Raw defect count (G) and smallest count (H) confuse count with rate.

distractorExplanations.a: G’s 10 defects are the most, but 10/80 is only 12.5%, below J’s 20%.
distractorExplanations.c: Lot size does not rank defect rate; F’s rate is 8%.
distractorExplanations.d: Fewest defects (H) is the lowest rate here (5%), not the highest.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A studio’s March costs: rent $2,400, utilities $360, clay and glaze $540. What percent of the $3,300 total is clay and glaze?
gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Total 2400+360+540=3300. Clay and glaze 540/3300≈16.4%. Utilities and rent are other slices. 540/2400 is percent of rent, not of total cost.

distractorExplanations.a: About 11% is roughly utilities’ share ($360), not clay and glaze.
distractorExplanations.b: About 73% is rent’s share, not the clay and glaze line.
distractorExplanations.d: Divides by the rent line instead of by the $3,300 total cost.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Among 200 riders, 90 named bus, 70 named bike, 40 named walk as their usual mode (one choice each). If a stacked bar uses those three counts, which reading is correct?

options.a: Bike is 50% of riders because 70 is close to half of 90+40
options.b: Walk is 40% of riders because the walk count is 40 people
options.c: Bus plus walk is 70% because 90 + 40 = 130 of an unknown base
options.d: Bus is 45% of riders because 90/200 = 0.45

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: The base is 200. Bus 90/200=45%, bike 35%, walk 20%. Treating a raw count as a percent (40 people → 40%) or changing the denominator to 90+40 are classic chart misreads.

distractorExplanations.a: 70/200 is 35%, not 50%; 90+40 is not the survey base.
distractorExplanations.b: 40 walkers are 20% of the 200-rider base, not a 40% share.
distractorExplanations.c: 130/200 is 65%, and the base is known (200), not unknown.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A city pool scanned weekday vs weekend entries (people): Mon 120, Tue 110, Sat 200, Sun 180. Lifeguards claim weekend days average at least 50% more entries than weekday days. Which verdict is supported?

options.a: True: weekend mean 190 vs weekday mean 115 is about a 65% premium
options.b: True: Sunday 180 is 50% above Monday 120, so the claim holds on one pair
options.c: False: 200 + 180 is not 50% above 120 + 110, so weekends lag
options.d: False: any Saturday below 250 entries falsifies a 50% weekend premium

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Weekday mean (120+110)/2=115. Weekend mean (200+180)/2=190. (190−115)/115≈65% which is at least 50%. The claim compares type-of-day averages, not one Sunday–Monday pair and not a 250-entry Saturday rule.

distractorExplanations.b: One pair (Sun vs Mon) is not the stated comparison of weekend vs weekday averages.
distractorExplanations.c: Weekend sums still far exceed weekday sums; weekends do not lag on this data.
distractorExplanations.d: The claim is about a 50% average premium over weekdays, not a 250-entry Saturday floor.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Three mural tasks list remaining hours and percent already done: Sky 6 h left, 50% done; Wall 5 h left, 20% done; Gate 12 h left, 40% done. Original hours = remaining / (1 − percent done). Which task had the largest original estimate?

options.a: Sky, because 6 / 0.50 = 12 original hours
options.b: Gate, because 12 / 0.60 = 20 original hours
options.c: Wall, because 5 / 0.20 = 25 original hours
options.d: Sky, because remaining hours alone rank original plans
