gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Original = remaining/(1−p). Sky 6/0.50=12; Wall 5/0.80=6.25; Gate 12/0.60=20. Gate is largest. Option c uses the done percent as the unfinished share, a common inversion.

distractorExplanations.a: Sky’s 12 original hours are less than Gate’s 20.
distractorExplanations.c: Wall’s unfinished share is 80%, so 5/0.80=6.25, not 5/0.20.
distractorExplanations.d: Remaining hours ignore percent complete; Sky’s 6 left is not the largest original.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Fund Cedar returned +8% then −2% in two years on a $10,000 start. Fund Maple returned +3% then +3%. Which pair of ending values is correct (interest compounded annually)?

options.a: Cedar $10,800 and Maple $10,600 after the two years
options.b: Cedar $10,584 and Maple $10,300 after the two years
options.c: Cedar $10,584 and Maple $10,609 after the two years
options.d: Cedar $10,000 and Maple $10,609 after the two years

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Cedar: 10000×1.08=10800, then ×0.98=10584. Maple: 10000×1.03²=10609. Adding 8% then subtracting 2% of the original (not of 10800) is the Cedar trap. Maple is not 6% of 10000 without compounding.

distractorExplanations.a: Cedar $10,800 is after year 1 only; Maple $10,600 skips compounding on the second 3%.
distractorExplanations.b: Cedar $10,584 is right, but Maple $10,300 is a single 3% increase, not two.
distractorExplanations.d: Cedar does not finish at the start value; the +8% then −2% path ends at $10,584.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A lab began each quarter with 80 kits. Kits discarded: Q1 6, Q2 9, Q3 5, Q4 8. Replacements arrived only after each quarter’s count. What were total discards, and which quarter discarded the most?

options.a: 24 discards, with Q1 the highest-discard quarter
options.b: 28 discards, with Q4 the highest-discard quarter
options.c: 80 discards in total, with Q2 the highest-discard quarter
options.d: 28 discards, with Q2 the highest-discard quarter

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: 6+9+5+8=28. Q2’s 9 is the peak. Opening stock 80 is not a discard total. Q1’s 6 and Q4’s 8 are below 9.

distractorExplanations.a: The sum is 28, not 24, and Q1’s 6 is not the peak.
distractorExplanations.b: 28 is the right sum, but Q4’s 8 is below Q2’s 9.
distractorExplanations.c: 80 is the opening stock each quarter, not the discard total, even though Q2 is the peak.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A scatter of dose D (mg) vs relief R (%) has fitted line R = 2D + 10. At D=12 the residual of one patient is −6. What was that patient’s actual R, and what does a negative residual mean here?

options.a: Actual R=28; the point sits 6 points below the line
options.b: Actual R=34; the point sits 6 points above the fitted line
options.c: Actual R=6; residual size equals the observed relief score
options.d: Actual R=40; the point sits 6 points above the fitted line

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Fitted R at D=12 is 2(12)+10=34. Residual = actual − fitted = −6, so actual = 28. Negative residual means observed below the line, not above, and not equal to 6% relief.

distractorExplanations.b: 34 is the fitted value; a negative residual puts the actual below 34, not above.
distractorExplanations.c: The residual is an error versus the line, not the patient’s relief score.
distractorExplanations.d: Adds 6 to the fitted 34; a negative residual means the actual value lies below the line.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Three outreach waves: Wave P reach 8,000 at 5% conversion; Wave Q reach 5,000 at 12%; Wave R reach 10,000 at 4%. Which wave produced the most conversions, and about how many?

options.a: Wave P, about 400
options.b: Wave Q, about 600
options.c: Wave R, about 400
options.d: Wave R, about 1,000

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Conversions: P 8000×0.05=400; Q 5000×0.12=600; R 10000×0.04=400. Q wins despite smaller reach. Using reach rank or a 10% round number for R are the traps.

distractorExplanations.a: P converts 8,000 × 5% = 400, which ties R and trails Q's 600.
distractorExplanations.c: R converts 10,000 × 4% = 400; the largest reach does not give the most conversions when its rate is lowest.
distractorExplanations.d: 1,000 is 10% of 10,000; R converts at 4%, which gives only 400.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A co-op sells honey at 40% margin on cost and beeswax tins at 25% margin on cost. Cost is $12 per honey jar and $8 per tin. Which pair of selling prices follows those cost margins?

options.a: Honey $4.80 and tins $2.00
options.b: Honey $12.40 and tins $8.25
options.c: Honey $16.80 and tins $10.00
options.d: Honey $20.00 and tins $10.67

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Price = cost × (1 + margin on cost). Honey 12 × 1.40 = $16.80; tins 8 × 1.25 = $10.00. Reporting the markup alone, adding cents instead of percent, or treating the margin as a share of price are the usual percent errors.

distractorExplanations.a: $4.80 and $2.00 are the markups alone (40% of $12 and 25% of $8); the selling price adds each markup to its cost.
distractorExplanations.b: Adding 40 cents and 25 cents treats “percent” as “cents” instead of taking 40% and 25% of each cost.
distractorExplanations.d: Dividing cost by (1 − margin) builds a margin on selling price; these margins are on cost, so multiply by 1.40 and 1.25.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Of 500 students, 180 play in band, 150 run track, and 60 do both. How many do neither activity, and how many do exactly one?

options.a: Neither 170 and exactly one 270
options.b: Neither 230 and exactly one 330
options.c: Neither 110 and exactly one 60
options.d: Neither 230 and exactly one 210

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Union = 180+150−60=270. Neither = 500−270=230. Exactly one = 270−60=210 (or 120 band-only + 90 track-only). Adding 180+150 without subtracting overlap overstates the union.

distractorExplanations.a: Union is 270, so neither is 230, not 170; exactly one is 210, not 270.
distractorExplanations.b: Exactly one cannot be 330 if the union itself is only 270.
distractorExplanations.c: The 60 overlap is both activities, not the exactly-one group.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: ER wait samples (minutes): Desk A 12, 18, 15, 21; Desk B 20, 14, 16, 18. Which desk has the higher mean wait, and by how many minutes?

options.a: Desk B by 0.5: mean 17 versus Desk A’s 16.5
options.b: Desk A by 0.5: mean 17 versus Desk B’s 16.5
options.c: Desk A by 3: using 21 versus 18 as the two means
options.d: The desks tie at a 16-minute mean wait

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: A: (12+18+15+21)/4=66/4=16.5. B: (20+14+16+18)/4=68/4=17. B is 0.5 minutes higher. Swapping the means or using a single reading as the mean are the traps.

distractorExplanations.b: A’s mean is 16.5, not 17; swapping desks reverses the 0.5-minute gap.
distractorExplanations.c: 21 and 18 are single observations, not the four-reading means.
distractorExplanations.d: 16.5 and 17 are not equal, so the desks do not tie.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A potter’s weekly cost is $400 fixed plus $6 per bowl. Bowls sell at $16. What is the weekly break-even quantity, and what is profit at 50 bowls?

options.a: Break-even 25 bowls; profit at 50 bowls is $500
options.b: Break-even 40 bowls; profit at 50 bowls is $100
options.c: Break-even 40 bowls; weekly profit at 50 bowls is $800
options.d: Break-even 67 bowls; profit at 50 bowls is $100

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Contribution $16−$6=$10 per bowl. Break-even 400/10=40. At 50 bowls, profit = 10×50 − 400 = $100. Using price instead of contribution (400/16=25) is a common error. $800 ignores variable cost.

distractorExplanations.a: 400/16=25 uses price, not contribution margin; 50×10−400 is $100, not $500.
distractorExplanations.c: Break-even 40 is right, but $800 is 50×16, which ignores $6 variable and $400 fixed.
distractorExplanations.d: 67 would be 400/6, dividing fixed cost by variable cost instead of by contribution.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Library checkouts this month: graphic novels 90, cookbooks 60, travel 30, poetry 20. Graphic novels are what percent of the 200 checkouts?
gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Total 90+60+30+20=200. Graphic novels 90/200=45%. Raw counts of 30, 60, or 90 are not percents of 200.

distractorExplanations.a: 30 travel checkouts are 15% of 200, and 30% is cookbooks’ share, not graphic novels’.
distractorExplanations.c: 60 is the cookbook count, not a percent; graphic novels are 90 of 200.
distractorExplanations.d: 90 is the graphic-novel count, not 90% of a 200-checkout base.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A software sprint budget is $48,000. Spent so far: design $12,000, build $18,000, test $6,000. Remaining work is estimated at 40% of the original budget. Which pair is correct?

options.a: Spent $30,000; remaining-work estimate $19,200
options.b: Spent $36,000; remaining-work estimate the full $48,000
options.c: Spent $36,000; remaining-work estimate $28,800
options.d: Spent $36,000; remaining-work estimate $19,200

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Spent = 12,000 + 18,000 + 6,000 = $36,000. The remaining-work estimate is 40% of the original $48,000 = $19,200, not the full budget and not the 60% complement ($28,800). Together the two figures reach $55,200, so the sprint is heading over budget.

distractorExplanations.a: The three spend lines sum to $36,000, not $30,000 (that omits test).
distractorExplanations.b: Spent $36,000 is right, but $48,000 is the original budget, not 40% of it.
distractorExplanations.c: $28,800 is 60% of $48,000, the complement of the 40% estimate; the spent share is actually 75%, and neither is the remaining-work figure.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: App-store reviews last month (pos/neu/neg): River 80/30/10; Harbor 50/40/10; Dune 40/20/40. Which app has the highest positive share of its own reviews?

options.a: River, because 80/120 ≈ 67% of its reviews are positive
options.b: Harbor, because 50 positives sit between the other two apps
options.c: Dune, because 40 negatives show the most engagement
options.d: Harbor, because 50/100 = 50% beats River’s 80 positives raw

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Totals: River 120, Harbor 100, Dune 100. Positive shares: River 80/120≈66.7%; Harbor 50%; Dune 40%. Raw positive counts or negative “engagement” do not rank positive share.

distractorExplanations.b: Harbor’s 50 positives are a 50% share, below River’s two-thirds.
distractorExplanations.c: Dune’s many negatives pull its positive share down to 40%.
distractorExplanations.d: Harbor’s 50% share does not beat River’s ~67%, even though Harbor’s base is 100.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Closing index points over four sessions: Cedar 250, 255, 248, 260; Maple 180, 198, 190, 207. Which fund had the larger percent gain from first close to last close?

options.a: Cedar, because 260 − 250 = 10 points beats Maple’s 27-point rise
options.b: Maple, because 207/180 − 1 = 15% while Cedar is only 4%
options.c: Cedar, because 260/250 − 1 = 4% is called the larger percent
options.d: They tie, because each fund gained exactly 10 index points

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Cedar: (260−250)/250=4%. Maple: (207−180)/180=15%. Maple’s percent gain is larger. A 10-point tie is false (Maple rose 27 points).

distractorExplanations.a: Percent change uses the starting base; Cedar’s +10 points is only 4% of 250.
distractorExplanations.c: 4% is Cedar’s percent gain, which is smaller than Maple’s 15%, not larger.
distractorExplanations.d: Cedar rose 10 points and Maple rose 27; they do not tie in points or percent.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: In a 300-commuter survey, 40 use only tram, 50 only ferry, 30 only bike, 20 tram+ferry not bike, 15 ferry+bike not tram, 10 tram+bike not ferry, 8 all three, and the rest use none of the three. How many use none?
gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Union = 40+50+30+20+15+10+8=173. None = 300−173=127. 165 would omit the 8 all-three riders from the union. 173 is the union, not the unused group.

distractorExplanations.a: The 8 is the all-three overlap, not the group that uses none of the modes.
distractorExplanations.c: Leaves the 8 all-three riders out of the union (165), so none comes out as 135 instead of 127.
distractorExplanations.d: 173 is the union, the commuters who use at least one mode; none is 300 − 173.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A maker’s revenue and costs ($ thousands): 2021 80 and 62; 2022 90 and 70; 2023 88 and 71. In which year was profit highest, and what was that profit?

options.a: 2021 at $18 thousand
options.b: 2022 at $90 thousand
options.c: 2023 at $17 thousand
options.d: 2022 at $20 thousand

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Profit = revenue − costs: 2021 18; 2022 20; 2023 17. Peak profit is 2022 at 20 thousand, not peak revenue. Reading revenue as profit is the main trap.

distractorExplanations.a: 2021 profit is $18 thousand (80 − 62), below 2022’s $20 thousand.
distractorExplanations.b: Peak revenue in 2022 is $90 thousand, but profit is the $20 thousand left after $70 thousand of costs.
distractorExplanations.c: 2023 profit is $17 thousand (88 − 71), the lowest of the three years.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Seed-packet sales by region (units × average price): North 400 × $6; South 250 × $8; West 300 × $7. Which region had the largest revenue?

options.a: North
options.b: South
options.c: West
options.d: North and South tie

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Revenue = units × average price: North 400 × 6 = $2,400; South 250 × 8 = $2,000; West 300 × 7 = $2,100. North leads; the highest price (South) does not win once volume is counted.

distractorExplanations.b: South has the highest price, but 250 × $8 = $2,000 trails North's 400 × $6 = $2,400.
distractorExplanations.c: West's 300 × $7 = $2,100 is second, still $300 below North's $2,400.
distractorExplanations.d: South's 250 × $8 is $2,000, not $2,400, so there is no tie; North leads on its own.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Three restoration tasks: Frame 10 days at 40% done; Canvas 6 days at 75% done; Gilding 8 days at 50% done. Remaining days = original × (1 − percent done). Which task has the most days left?

options.a: Gilding, 4 days
options.b: Canvas, 4.5 days
options.c: Frame, 6 days
options.d: Frame, 10 days

distractorExplanations.a: Gilding's 8 × 0.50 = 4 days left is correct, but Frame's 6 days left is more.
distractorExplanations.b: 4.5 multiplies by the percent done (6 × 0.75); Canvas has 6 × 0.25 = 1.5 days left, the least of the three.
distractorExplanations.d: 10 days is Frame's original estimate; 40% is done, so 10 × 0.60 = 6 days remain.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Ticket booths by pier (sellers × average weekly sales): East 8 × $900; Mid 5 × $1,200; West 10 × $700. Which pier has the largest weekly booth total?

options.a: Mid
options.b: West
options.c: East
options.d: East and West tie

distractorExplanations.a: Mid has the highest average, but 5 × $1,200 = $6,000 is the lowest total of the three piers.
distractorExplanations.b: West has the most sellers, but 10 × $700 = $7,000 is $200 below East's $7,200.
distractorExplanations.d: West's 10 × $700 is $7,000, not $7,200, so East leads by $200; there is no tie.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Unit cost and selling price: Loom $40 / $55; Kiln $70 / $90; Press $25 / $40. Which product has the highest contribution per unit (price − cost)?

distractorExplanations.b: Lowest cost (Press) still yields only $15 contribution.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A 200-person co-op: Kitchen 50, Front 40, Cellar 30, Delivery 80. Delivery is what percent of staff, and Kitchen plus Front together?

options.d: Delivery 25% and Kitchen+Front 40%

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A stall’s costs were $4,000 in April, then rose $250 each month. What were June costs, and what was the April–June total?

options.a: June $4,250 and three-month total $12,750
options.b: June $4,500 and three-month total $12,750
options.c: June $4,500 and three-month total $13,500
options.d: June $4,750 and three-month total $12,750

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: April 4000, May 4250, June 4500. Total 4000+4250+4500=12750. June is two steps of $250, not one. 3×4500=13500 pretends every month is June. July would be 4750.

distractorExplanations.a: June is the second $250 step ($4,500), not May’s $4,250.
distractorExplanations.c: June $4,500 is right, but 3×$4,500 ignores that April and May were lower.
distractorExplanations.d: $4,750 would be July (third step); June is only two steps above April.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Two radio spots: Spot K cost $2,000 and produced 250 visits; Spot L cost $3,000 and produced 450 visits. Which spot had the lower cost per visit, and what is that cost?

options.a: Spot K at $8.00, because 2000/250 = 8 and K spent less overall
options.b: Spot K at $0.125, because 250/2000 = 0.125
options.c: Spot L at about $6.67, because 3000/450 ≈ 6.67 versus K’s $8
options.d: Spot K at about $6.67 per visit

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: K: 2000/250=$8. L: 3000/450=$6.67. L is cheaper per visit even though it spent more in total. Lower total spend is not lower unit cost.

distractorExplanations.a: K’s $8 per visit is higher than L’s ~$6.67; lower total spend is not the metric.
distractorExplanations.b: 250/2000 is visits per dollar, not cost per visit; K’s cost per visit is $8.
distractorExplanations.d: $6.67 belongs to L, not K; swapping the unit costs flips the winner.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Quiz scores: 82, 90, 76, 88, 84. What is the mean, and is it higher than the median?

options.a: Mean 88; yes, because 88 is the largest listed score
options.b: Mean 84; no, because the median is 90
options.c: Mean 82; yes, because 82 is the first listed score
options.d: Mean 84; no, because the ordered median is also 84

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Sum 82+90+76+88+84=420; mean 420/5=84. Ordered: 76,82,84,88,90; median 84. Mean equals median, so the mean is not higher. Using 88 or 90 as median/mean confuses a single high score with the center.

distractorExplanations.a: 88 is one score, not the mean; the mean is 84.
distractorExplanations.b: The mean is 84, but the median is the third ordered value 84, not 90.
distractorExplanations.c: 82 is the first listed score, not the mean of five.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A cannery’s cases shipped: Anchovy 120, 100, 110; Brine 80, 90, 70; Citrus 60, 65, 75 for three periods. Which line had the largest three-period total?

options.b: Brine with 330 cases
options.c: Citrus with 200 cases
options.d: Anchovy with 120 cases

distractorExplanations.b: Brine totals 240, not 330; 330 is Anchovy’s sum.
distractorExplanations.c: Citrus’s 200 is the smallest three-period total, not the largest.
distractorExplanations.d: 120 is only period 1 for Anchovy, not the three-period sum.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Devices assembled: Radio 120 units, 6 returns; Clock 80, 8; Meter 200, 10. Which device has the highest return rate?

options.a: Meter, because 10 returns is the largest return count
options.b: Clock, because 8/80 = 10% beats the others’ 5%
options.c: Radio, because 120 units is a mid-size assembly lot
options.d: Meter, because 200 units is the largest assembly lot

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Rates: Radio 6/120=5%; Clock 8/80=10%; Meter 10/200=5%. Clock has the highest rate. Largest return count or largest lot is not the highest rate.

distractorExplanations.a: Meter’s 10 returns are 5% of 200, tying Radio and trailing Clock.
distractorExplanations.c: Lot size does not rank return rate; Radio’s rate is 5%.
distractorExplanations.d: Largest lot (Meter) has a 5% rate, not the highest.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Cost and price: Mug $9 / $15; Bowl $12 / $20; Jug $8 / $14. If 20 mugs, 10 bowls, and 5 jugs sell, which product contributes the most total dollar margin?

options.a: Bowl
options.b: Jug
options.c: Mug
options.d: Mug and Jug tie

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Unit margins: Mug 6, Bowl 8, Jug 6. Totals: 20×6=120; 10×8=80; 5×6=30. Mugs win on volume. Highest unit margin (Bowl) does not win total dollars here.

distractorExplanations.a: Bowl has the highest unit margin ($8), but 10 × $8 = $80 trails the mugs' 20 × $6 = $120.
distractorExplanations.b: Jug's $14 price hides a $6 unit margin; 5 × $6 = $30 is the smallest total of the three.
distractorExplanations.d: Mugs and jugs share a $6 unit margin, but 20 mugs give $120 and 5 jugs only $30; the question asks for total dollars.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A press’s revenue grew 10% in year 1 and 20% in year 2. Starting revenue was $50,000. Which pair is correct for year-2 ending revenue and the two-year total growth rate from the start?

options.a: Ending $60,000 and two-year growth 30%
options.b: Ending $66,000 and two-year growth 30%
options.c: Ending $55,000 and two-year growth 32%
options.d: Ending $66,000 and two-year growth 32%

distractorExplanations.a: $60,000 is 20% on the start, skipping the 10% year; 30% adds the percents instead of compounding.
distractorExplanations.b: Ending $66,000 is right, but 10%+20% = 30% understates the compounded 32%.
distractorExplanations.c: $55,000 is the year-1 level, not the year-2 end.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A marina fuel dock posted liters sold: diesel 2,400; gasoline 1,800; oil mix 600. Diesel is what percent of the 4,800-liter total, and gasoline plus oil mix together?

options.a: Diesel 50% and gasoline+oil 50%

options.c: Diesel 50% and gasoline+oil only 18%
options.d: Diesel 80% and gasoline+oil 50%

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Total 2400+1800+600=4800. Diesel 2400/4800=50%. Gasoline+oil 2400/4800=50%. 24% would treat 2400 as a percent. 18% would be 1800/100 as if 1800 were 18%.

distractorExplanations.b: 2,400 liters is not 24% of 4,800; it is 50%.
distractorExplanations.c: Diesel 50% is right, but gasoline+oil is also 50% (2,400 liters), not 18%.
distractorExplanations.d: 80% would require 3,840 diesel liters; the dock sold 2,400.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A kiosk’s week-1 sales were $9,000 and then rose $600 each week. What were week-4 sales, and what was the four-week total?

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A sauce brand’s share (%) is modeled as M(t)=5×(1.2)^t, t = years after launch. Which pair is correct for M(0) and M(2)?

distractorExplanations.a: The model’s t=0 value is 5, not 0; 7.2 is the right M(2) but paired with a wrong intercept.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Closers and deals: Nia 40 calls, 8 deals; Omar 25 calls, 10 deals; Pri 50 calls, 9 deals. Who has the highest deals-per-call rate?

options.a: Pri, because 50 calls is the heaviest activity listed
options.b: Nia, because 40 calls is a mid-size effort

options.d: Omar, because 10/25 = 0.40 is the top rate

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Rates: Nia 8/40=0.20; Omar 10/25=0.40; Pri 9/50=0.18. Omar converts best. Most calls or a middle deal count is not the rate.

distractorExplanations.a: Pri’s 50 calls yield only a 0.18 rate, the lowest of the three.
distractorExplanations.b: Nia’s 8/40 = 0.20 conversion rate still trails Omar’s 0.40.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A greenhouse logged trays: basil 90, mint 40, thyme 30, sage 20. Basil is what percent of the 180 trays, and mint+thyme together?

options.a: Basil 50% and mint+thyme about 39%
options.b: Basil 90% and mint+thyme 70%
options.c: Basil 50% and mint+thyme 70%
options.d: Basil about 18% and mint+thyme about 39%

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Total 90+40+30+20=180. Basil 90/180=50%. Mint+thyme 70/180≈38.9%. Treating 90 and 70 as percents ignores the 180 base. 18% would be 90/500 or similar.

distractorExplanations.b: 90 and 70 are tray counts, not percents of 180.
distractorExplanations.c: Basil 50% is right, but mint+thyme is 70/180≈39%, not 70%.
distractorExplanations.d: 18% is not 90/180; basil is half the trays.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A help desk closed tickets: Day 1 40, Day 2 36, Day 3 44, Day 4 40. Which statement about the four-day mean and range is correct?

options.a: Mean 44 and range 8
options.b: Mean 40 and range 8
options.c: Mean 40 and range 4
options.d: Mean 36 and range 8

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Mean (40+36+44+40)/4=40. Range 44−36=8. Peak or trough as the mean is the trap. Range needs max−min, not a single step from 40 to 36.

distractorExplanations.a: 44 is the peak, not the mean; the mean is 40.
distractorExplanations.c: Mean 40 is right, but the range uses 44 and 36, a spread of 8, not 4.
distractorExplanations.d: 36 is the weakest day, not the four-day mean of 40 tickets.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: Monthly ad spend and sales ($ thousands): M1 8 and 80; M2 10 and 90; M3 12 and 96. Sales per ad dollar fell each month. Which set of sales-per-ad-dollar figures is correct?
gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Sales per ad dollar: 80/8=10; 90/10=9; 96/12=8, which falls each month. Repeating sales or spend as the ratio, or reversing the decline, misses the division.

distractorExplanations.a: The ratios fall (10, 9, 8), not rise; 80/8 is $10, not $8.
distractorExplanations.b: Sales thousands are the numerator, not the ratio; spend must divide them.
distractorExplanations.d: Spend thousands are the denominator, not the sales-per-dollar figures.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A foundry’s shift output (parts): Night 120, 110, 130; Swing 90, 100, 95. Which shift has the higher three-shift total, and by how many parts?

options.a: Swing by 75 parts

options.c: The shifts tie at 360 parts
options.d: Night by 75 parts

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Night 120+110+130=360; Swing 90+100+95=285; gap 75. Reporting 360 as the gap or reversing who leads are the traps. They do not tie.

distractorExplanations.a: Swing’s 285 trails Night; reversing the labels flips the leader.
distractorExplanations.b: 360 is Night’s total, not the 75-part difference.
distractorExplanations.c: 360 and 285 are not equal, so the shifts do not tie.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A two-part dashboard asks: (i) did on-time flights rise from May to June, and (ii) did cancellations fall? May: 420 on-time, 18 canceled; June: 405 on-time, 12 canceled. Which pair of answers is correct?

options.a: On-time rose and cancellations fell
options.b: On-time rose and cancellations rose
options.c: On-time fell and cancellations fell
options.d: On-time fell while cancellations rose

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: On-time 420→405 is a fall. Cancellations 18→12 is a fall. Both falling is the supported pair. Direction errors on either series produce the other three options.

distractorExplanations.a: On-time counts fell from 420 to 405; they did not rise.
distractorExplanations.b: On-time fell, and cancellations also fell rather than rose.
distractorExplanations.d: Cancellations fell from 18 to 12; they did not rise.

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.prompt: A print shop’s unit cost and price: Poster $4 / $9; Zine $6 / $10. Fixed weekly costs are $300. If the shop sells 40 posters and 20 zines, which pair is correct?

options.a: Contribution $400 and profit $100
options.b: Contribution $280 and profit $280
options.c: Contribution $560 and profit $260
options.d: Contribution $280 and profit −$20

gmat-focus-readiness-check-data-insights.explanation: Poster margin $5 × 40 = $200. Zine margin $4 × 20 = $80. Contribution $280. Profit 280−300=−$20. Skipping fixed cost reports $280 profit. Adding prices 40×9+20×10=560 is not contribution.

distractorExplanations.a: Poster margin is $5, not $10; 40×10 would overstate contribution.
distractorExplanations.b: $280 is contribution, not profit; the $300 fixed cost still must be subtracted.
distractorExplanations.c: $560 is total revenue (40 × 9 + 20 × 10); contribution subtracts unit costs first.
